q.t: Fill in: She ate ___ apple.
q.e: ‘apple’ starts with a vowel sound, so ‘an’.

q.t: Fill in: He has ___ cat.
q.e: ‘cat’ starts with a consonant sound and is singular and new → ‘a’.

q.t: Fill in: ___ sun rises in the east.
q.e: There is only one sun, so ‘the’.

q.t: Fill in: I waited for ___ hour.
q.e: The h in ‘hour’ is silent; the first sound is ‘ow’, a vowel sound → an.

q.t: Fill in: She studies at ___ university.
q.e: ‘university’ begins with a ‘yoo’ sound — a consonant sound → a.

q.t: Fill in: ___ Ganga is a holy river.
q.e: Rivers take ‘the’.

q.t: Fill in: He is ___ best player in the team.
q.e: Superlatives take ‘the’ — there is only one best.

q.t: Fill in: ___ books on this shelf are mine. (far away)
q.e: Plural (books) and far → those.

q.t: Fill in: Do you have ___ questions?
q.e: In questions that are left open, use ‘any’.

q.t: Fill in: We play ___ cricket every evening.
q.e: Names of games take no article.

q.t: Fill in: He is ___ honest man.
q.e: Silent h: ‘honest’ begins with an ‘o’ sound → an.

q.t: Fill in: I saw a dog in the park. ___ dog was barking.
q.e: Second mention — the listener now knows which dog → the.

q.t: Fill in: She is ___ European.
q.e: ‘European’ starts with a ‘yoo’ sound (a consonant sound) → a.

q.t: Fill in: He wants to become ___ MLA.
q.e: MLA is spoken ‘em-el-ay’, starting with a vowel sound → an.

q.t: Fill in: ___ Himalayas are in the north.
q.e: Mountain ranges take ‘the’.

q.t: Fill in: Mount Everest is in ___ Nepal.
q.e: Names of most countries take no article (but: the USA, the UK).

q.t: Fill in: There is ___ milk in the jug. (enough for tea)
q.e: Milk is uncountable; ‘a little’ = some, enough.

q.t: Fill in: ___ student must carry an ID card.
q.e: ‘student’ is singular and ‘must’ works for each → Every (or Each). ‘All/Many/Both’ need a plural noun.

q.t: Fill in: She plays ___ guitar beautifully.
q.e: Musical instruments take ‘the’ when we talk of playing them.

q.t: Fill in: Would you like ___ juice?
q.e: An offer expects ‘yes’, so use ‘some’ even in a question. Juice is uncountable, so not ‘a’ or ‘many’.

q.t: Fill in: He goes to ___ church every Sunday. (to pray)
q.e: Going to a place for its main purpose (praying at church) — no article.

q.t: Fill in: The plumber went to ___ church to fix a pipe.
q.e: He is not going to pray — it is just a building he visits, so ‘the’.

q.t: Fill in: ___ USA is a large country.
q.e: ‘States’ is a common noun, so the full name takes ‘the’: the USA, the UK.

q.t: Fill in: He gave me ___ one-rupee coin.
q.e: ‘one’ begins with a ‘w’ sound — a consonant sound → a.

q.t: Fill in: ___ honesty is the best policy.
q.e: An abstract idea in general takes no article.

q.t: Fill in: She reads ___ Hindu every morning. (a newspaper)
q.e: Names of newspapers take ‘the’.

q.t: Fill in: ___ of the two roads leads to the station. (one or the other)
q.e: ‘Either’ = one of two. ‘Both’ would need ‘lead’ and means the two together.

q.t: Fill in: I have read ___ the books in this series.
q.e: ‘all the’ + plural noun. ‘every’ and ‘each’ take a singular noun and no ‘the’.

q.t: Find the error: An university was opened in our town.
q.e: It is the sound that matters: ‘yoo-niversity’ starts with a consonant sound → a.

q.t: Fill in: He is ___ only son of his parents.
q.e: ‘only’ makes it one particular person → the.

q.t: Fill in: It was ___ unique experience.
q.e: ‘unique’ starts with a ‘yoo’ sound → a, even though it is spelt with u.

q.t: Fill in: He was taken to ___ hospital after the accident. (as a patient)
q.e: Going to hospital for its purpose (treatment) — no article (Indian/British use).

q.t: Fill in: ___ Andamans are a group of islands.
q.e: Groups of islands take ‘the’.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
q.e: ‘Neither’ + singular noun + singular verb. (With ‘of’: neither of the answers is …)

q.t: Fill in: I have ___ time to waste. (none at all)
q.e: ‘no’ = not any. ‘any’ only works in a negative sentence (I don't have any time).

q.t: Fill in: Rohan is ___ Einstein of our class.
q.e: Here a famous name is used to mean ‘the genius’ of the class — one particular person, so ‘the’.

q.t: Find the error: The honesty of the boy impressed everyone.
q.e: ‘honesty’ usually takes no article, but here it is a particular honesty — of the boy — so ‘the’ is correct.

q.t: Fill in: He has ___ X-ray report with him.
q.e: ‘X’ is spoken ‘eks’, starting with a vowel sound → an.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Each of the boys has a bicycle.
Each of the boys have a bicycle.
Each of the boy has a bicycle.
q.e: ‘Each of the’ + plural noun, but ‘each’ is the subject — singular verb ‘has’.

q.t: Fill in: ___ rich should help ___ poor.
q.e: ‘the’ + adjective means all people of that kind: the rich = rich people, the poor = poor people.
